description.text: Ryder System, Inc. (Ryder) is a leading provider of outsourced logistics and transportation services throughout North America. We offer port-to-door solutions that integrate every step of the supply chain, including international inbound flows and cross-border logistics, fleet and transportation management, warehousing, manufacturing support and multi-channel final delivery. Our complementary business segments provide a broad range of value-added solutions, which provides our customers with a seamless, end-to-end logistics network designed to reduce complexity and improve speed, reliability and efficiency across the entire flow of goods. Ryder connects every link in the supply chain, moving products smoothly from ports and suppliers all the way to customers’ doorsteps as illustrated below. We report our financial performance based on three business segments: (1) Fleet Management Solutions (FMS), which provides full service leasing, commercial rental and vehicle maintenance services; (2) Supply Chain Solutions (SCS), which provides fully integrated logistics solutions; and (3) Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS), which provides turnkey transportation solutions, including dedicated vehicles, professional drivers, management and administrative support. Dedicated transportation services provided as part of an operationally integrated, multi-service supply chain solution to SCS customers are primarily reported in the SCS business segment.

about.description_short: Ryder System, Inc. (NYSE: R) is a nearly $13 billion leading provider of outsourced logistics and transportation services throughout the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Ryder offers supply chain, dedicated transportation, and fleet management solutions that integrate every step of the supply chain port-to-door, including cross-border logistics, fleet and transportation management, warehousing and distribution, and final delivery to customers' doorsteps. Ryder's broad portfolio of services encompasses managed transportation, freight brokerage, dedicated contract carriage with professional drivers, full-service fleet leasing and maintenance, commercial truck rental, automation and robotics, digital technologies, contract manufacturing and packaging, omnichannel retail fulfillment including e-commerce and last-mile delivery, and used vehicle sales.

analysis_md:
# R — Ryder System, Inc.
Engine 5.5.0 run, 2026-10-20. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
North American outsourced logistics and transportation company (SIC 7510), ~$12.7B revenue: Fleet Management Solutions (full-service leasing, maintenance, commercial rental, used-vehicle sales), Dedicated Transportation Solutions, and Supply Chain Solutions (~320 warehouses). Management said on the Q2 2026 call that over 90% of revenue is contractual, and Q2 2026 was its seventh consecutive quarter of comparable EPS growth: comparable EPS $3.73 (+12% YoY), total revenue $3.35B (+5%), ROE 17%, and non-GAAP free cash flow of $684M for the first half of 2026 (vs $461M in H1 2025, per the release's Corporate Financial Information section). Full-year 2026 guidance raised at Q2: comparable EPS $14.40–$14.80, operating revenue growth ~3%, OCF ~$2.7B and free cash flow $700–$800M (Q2 2026 earnings release, July 23, 2026). Q3 2026 reports October 22, 2026, with Q3 comparable EPS guided to $4.00–$4.20 vs $3.57 a year earlier.

## Owner's earnings
- Base OE/share: **$-10.40** (source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share); latest FY OE/share **$10.05**; latest FY OE total $420,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json).
- **OE-positive years (last 5): 2/5.** The pattern is the fleet capex cycle, from financials_history.csv: FY2023 OCF $2,353M vs capex $3,234M → OE $-925M ($-19.90/share); FY2024 OCF $2,265M vs capex $2,683M → OE $-460M ($-10.40/share); FY2025 OCF $2,594M vs capex $2,135M → OE $420M ($10.05/share). Capex here is `PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets` — revenue-earning vehicles — so the conservative definition (OCF − capex − SBC, SBC $39M in FY2025) charges all fleet growth against owner's earnings.
- F sub-type: **no_cash_generation** (sum of the last 3 fiscal years, the median window). No scenario table is produced — with a negative normalized base there is no supportable OE DCF, no IV@15% and no implied IRR. The engine note is explicit: the latest year alone being positive is a flag to investigate, not a pass.
- That investigation: capex is genuinely falling as management shrinks the rental fleet (rental utilization back to the 75% target on a 15% smaller average fleet in Q2 2026) and shifts toward less capital-intensive contractual business. fundamentals.json's TTM through Q2 2026 shows OCF $2,451M, capex $1,764M, FCF $687M ($17.07/share) — positive on a cash basis. But ttm.py exits non-zero — Ryder files no post-FY YTD share-based-compensation fact in its 10-Qs since the 2025-12-31 fiscal year end, so no filing-direct TTM owner's-earnings figure can be built, and no base_override can be declared from figures ttm.py did not produce. The median base stands, and it is negative.
- Balance sheet: net debt $7,447M at FY2025 (debt_current $819M + debt_lt $6,826M − cash $198M in the CSV, reconciling to dcf_numbers.json), plus lease liabilities of $1,035M. Price $237.00 (nasdaq_quote_api); market cap $9,907.3M on 41,803,000 diluted shares; the cover-page count is 38,346,868 as of 2026-06-30, inside the engine's tolerance (dei ratio 1.09, no share-basis flag).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate
Justification: Scale network and long-term contractual revenue give real switching friction, but the model is capital-intensive, pricing is contested by Penske/Enterprise and private fleets, and revenue growth has stalled.
- FOR: Scale North American network: ~240,000 vehicles under management and ~800 maintenance locations (company profile, Oct 2026) — density smaller rivals cannot replicate; long-term contractual model: over 90% of revenue contractual per management on the Q2 2026 call, seventh consecutive quarter of comparable EPS growth; integrated offer — Fleet Management, Dedicated Transportation and Supply Chain (~320 warehouses, ~100M sq ft) embedded in customer operations, raising switching costs.
- AGAINST: Capital intensity: fleet capex exceeded operating cash flow in FY2023 and FY2024 and has consumed nearly all of it for a decade — owner's earnings positive in only 2 of the last 5 years; freight-cycle and used-vehicle-price exposure (rental utilization and used tractor/truck pricing swing earnings; FY2025 revenue +0.23% YoY, 3-yr revenue CAGR 1.78% in dcf_numbers.json); Penske, Enterprise and customers' own private fleets cap pricing, and leverage is structural (net debt $7,447M plus $1,035M lease liabilities).
- ROIC evidence: the engine could not compute an ROIC proxy or recent gross margins — operating-income and COGS tags are null in EDGAR for Ryder — so there is no filing-direct evidence of returns above the cost of capital; ROE was 13.2% / 15.7% / 16.3% in FY2023–25 (fundamentals.json), respectable but levered. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years (dcf_numbers.json).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and exits non-zero — no post-FY YTD SBC fact is filed in Ryder's 10-Qs since the 2025-12-31 year end, so no filing-direct TTM OE exists. The Q2 2026 evidence was checked instead: comparable EPS $3.73 (+12%), management's non-GAAP FCF of $684M for H1 2026, and TTM FCF $687M in fundamentals.json (on the plain OCF − capex basis fundamentals.json shows $272M for Q2 2026 alone; management's non-GAAP measure is a different definition and a half-year period, not the quarter) — the direction is improving, but none of it is a ttm.py owner's-earnings figure the score may be pinned to. Median base retained.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 6.3%/yr): real and already credited — the engine applied the +5pp share-count adjustment to the revenue growth components only (g_blend 6.78%), and diluted shares fell from 53,508,000 (FY2021) to 41,803,000 (FY2025) in the CSV. Q2 2026 added a new 2M-share repurchase authorization and an 11% dividend increase (fundamentals.json: buybacks TTM $590M, DPS TTM $3.64). Not double-counted in the verdict; with a negative base it changes no tier.

## Thoughts / method range
- The OE model's answer is a statement about fit as much as about Ryder: a lessor whose capex *is* its product will show negative owner's earnings in any fleet-investment window and strongly positive ones when capex pauses — FY2020 OE/share was $19.19 and FY2025 $10.05 in the CSV, on the same business. The median window (FY2023–25) happened to catch the heaviest investment years ($3,234M and $2,683M capex) plus the first year of the downturn in spend.
- The equity story the market is pricing at $237.00 (JPMorgan upgraded to Overweight on October 5, 2026, target $298) is the comparable-EPS / ROE / buyback story: $14.40–$14.80 of guided 2026 comparable EPS at ~16x, ROE 17–18%, and a shrinking share count. None of that contradicts the F: it says the cash the fleet throws off after replacing and growing the fleet was negative on the normalized window this method capitalizes.
- If capex stays at the FY2025/TTM run-rate (~$1.8–2.1B) against ~$2.5–2.7B of OCF, a future run's median window turns positive and this name re-scores mechanically — that is the thing to watch, starting with the October 22, 2026 Q3 print and its capex guide.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (no_cash_generation; no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings — OE DCF not supportable)
- Confidence: **low** (the negative-median arithmetic is solid, but the OE/capex model fits a fleet lessor poorly — capex is the revenue-earning asset, and the latest FY and TTM cash figures are already positive)
- One-liner: Contractual fleet/logistics platform with a moderate 5/10 moat but no positive normalized owner's earnings — fleet capex consumed OCF in the median window (median OE/share $-10.40 vs latest FY $+10.05) — Tier F on the OE model at $237.00; the equity story rests on comparable EPS ($14.40–$14.80 guided for 2026) and buybacks, not OE.
